title: Carrova recipe (schema v2)
description: Declarative description of one app: how to detect it and which items (files/dirs) can move. Data only: no code, no commands, no absolute paths. Paths are (semantic root, relative path) pairs. v2 adds item-level `handler` (name of a built-in Carrova handler that captures/applies the item instead of raw file copies) and recipe-level `processes` (extra process names that count as the app running). Command fields (`export` / `import`) are never accepted. The Rust loader (carrova-recipe) applies additional semantic checks this schema cannot express: unique item ids, unique recipe ids across the tree, category == parent dir name, app dir name == id, exclude globs must compile.

schema.description: Recipe schema version. Must be 2 for this schema (v1 recipes validate against recipe.v1.json).

id.description: App id, lowercase kebab-case, unique across all recipes. Must equal the app directory name.

category.description: Category, lowercase kebab-case. Must equal the parent directory name (recipes/<category>/<id>/).

detect.description: Detection rules per OS. The app is detected if ANY rule for the current OS matches. v1 requires `linux`; `windows` / `macos` are accepted for forward compatibility.

processes.description: Extra process names (daemons, helpers) that count as the app running for `requires_closed` items, in addition to the `binary` detect rules. Bare names, no path separators.

items.description: Selectable items. Item ids must be unique within the recipe (checked by the loader).

bareName.description: Executable or process name: not empty, no `/`, `\` or NUL.

handler.description: Built-in handler. gpg-keyring: GnuPG public keys + ownertrust via `gpg --export` / `--import`.

semanticRoot.description: OS-neutral anchor resolved by the platform adapter.

relPath.description: Path relative to a semantic root. `/` separators; no leading `/` or `~`, no backslash, no NUL, no drive letter, no `..` component, not empty (after dropping `.` components).

detectRule.description: Exactly one of `binary` (bare executable name looked up on the search path) or `path` (exists, any kind, symlinks not followed).

flags.description: All fields optional. Defaults: portability=same_os, sensitive=false, requires_closed=false, default=true — except that sensitive and unmovable items default to OFF, and an explicit `default: true` on them is rejected.

portability.description: same_os: only restorable on the same OS family. cross_os: OS-neutral content. v1: everything is same_os.

sensitive.description: Secrets (keys, tokens, credential stores). Off by default and needs explicit confirmation.

requires_closed.description: The app must not be running while this item is captured/applied (databases, lock files).

default.description: Pre-selected in the picker. Effective default: true, or false when sensitive/unmovable.

paths.description: Files/dirs that make up the item (for handler items: the files the handler mutates). Required (non-empty) unless the item is unmovable.

exclude.description: Globs (`*` does not cross `/`, `**` does) matched against the path relative to the item path and relative to the semantic root. A matching directory excludes its subtree.

unmovable.description: Reason the item cannot move (e.g. OS-bound secret). Shown greyed out, never captured.

handler.description: Capture/apply via this built-in handler instead of copying raw files. `paths` then declare the files the handler mutates on the receiver (dry-run plan + rollback backup). Not allowed on unmovable items.
